title: THE GOD WHO CARRIES HIS PEOPLE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then I said to you, "Do not be terrified; do not be afraid of them. The Lord your God, who is going before you, will fight for you, as he did for you in Egypt, before your very eyes, and in the wilderness. There you saw how the Lord your God carried you, as a father carries his son, all the way you went until you reached this place." - Deut 1:29-31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses recalls how he pleaded with the fearful people: "Do not be terrified... The Lord your God, who is going before you, will fight for you." He pointed them back to what God had already done — fighting for them in Egypt, providing in the wilderness. And then he gives one of the most tender images in all of Scripture: God "carried you, as a father carries his son, all the way you went."

What a picture of God's love. Through all the wilderness years, God had not merely walked beside His people; He had carried them, the way a father lifts up a weary child and bears him along. When they were too tired to go on, too weak to make it themselves, He carried them. Every step of the journey, His fatherly strength was underneath them.

This is the God we so easily forget when fear takes over. The One the people accused of hating them was actually the Father who had tenderly carried them the whole way. If we could only remember how He has carried us, our fears would lose their grip. Look back over your own journey — the times you did not know how you would make it through, and somehow you did. That was God carrying you.

And He carries His people still. Isaiah pictures God saying He will carry us even to our old age and grey hairs (Isa 46:4). In Christ, we see the Father's heart most clearly — the Good Shepherd who lays the lost sheep on His shoulders and carries it home rejoicing (Luke 15:5). Whatever lies ahead, you do not have to face it in your own strength. The God who has carried you this far will carry you still. Rest in the arms of your Father.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Can you look back and see how God has carried you through hard times?
2. How does the image of God carrying you like a father change your fears?
3. What burden do you need to rest in your Father's carrying arms today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Loving Father, thank You that You have carried me all this way, like a father carrying his child. When I am weak and afraid, remind me that Your strength is underneath me, and help me rest in Your arms. Amen.
